ITEM.PTXT: An ultra-lightweight, high-rigidity magnesium alloy cylinder head cover has been adopted. It is installed to the cylinder head with fixed-torque tightening, distributing the tightening load evenly to ensure sealing performance. Furthermore, the baffle plate shape in the PCV chamber has been optimized and the PCV valve flow rate has been optimized, reducing oil carry-over and oil deterioration.

The cylinder head cover gasket is made of acrylic rubber with excellent heat resistance, ensuring sufficient reliability. Also, the spark plug tube gaskets have been integrated to improve serviceability.
An aluminum alloy cylinder head with excellent thermal conductivity has been adopted. Weight has been reduced by reducing the number of parts and making the walls thinner.

A metal 2-layer type cylinder head gasket has been adopted. The oil hole seal bead dimensions and water passage hole shapes have been optimized, and shims have been provided around the cylinder bores to increase the seal surface width, ensuring gas sealing performance and durability.

Vertical intake ports have been adopted and the valve included angle has been reduced to 27.5°, achieving both compactness and optimized intake efficiency. Also, low to medium speed torque has been ensured by using long intake ports.

A slant squish combustion chamber has been adopted. By slanting the squish area, masking around the valves is improved, increasing the intake air volume and the combustion speed in the latter half of combustion. This improves knock resistance and combustion efficiency.

By installing the fuel injectors in the cylinder head ports, the distance from the injectors to the intake valves has been shortened, reducing fuel adhesion to the intake ports and reducing HC emissions.
Cooling performance has been ensured by adopting a concentrated longitudinal flow system for the water jacket of the cylinder head and optimizing the jacket shape around the combustion chambers.
The structure has been simplified by building the water outlet into the rear end of the cylinder head and the water bypass pipe under the exhaust ports of the cylinder head.
By adopting an engine cover with sound insulation material, appearance and quietness have been improved.
An aluminum alloy cylinder block with cast-in thin cast iron liners has been adopted to reduce weight.

An aluminum alloy crankcase has been adopted. Integrating the stiffener ensures rigidity and reduces vibration. Also, friction has been reduced by giving the area around the balance shafts in the crankcase a cover shape that reduces the flow of oil onto the balance shafts.

An oil pan made of rust-resistant steel sheet has been adopted. By making the volume of the oil pan bottom large and lowering the oil level, oil agitation by the balance shafts, etc. has been reduced, reducing friction.
The water jacket is an open deck type, and the jacket has been made shallow to improve warm-up performance.

The cylinder head bolt counterbores have been made shallow to improve the roundness of the cylinder block, reducing friction and improving fuel economy, and the head gasket structure has been optimized to take bore deformation during assembly into account. Furthermore, bore deformation is also addressed by increasing the rigidity of the bore outer wall ribs.
By increasing the thickness of the transmission mounting flange and the crankcase mounting flange, the rigidity of the cylinder block has been improved and vibration and noise have been reduced.
An aluminum alloy cylinder block with cast-in thin cast iron liners has been adopted.
Oil from the cylinder head is returned to the oil pan from outside the journals so that the oil does not directly hit the crankshaft, reducing friction.
High rigidity has been achieved by curving the skirt and optimizing the positions of the side ribs.
Compactness has been achieved by mounting accessory parts directly to the cylinder block.

By providing a water jacket spacer, made of a resin material with excellent heat resistance and molding accuracy, in the water jacket of the cylinder block, the temperature distribution of the cylinder bore walls has been optimized, reducing friction.

The water jacket spacer suppresses the coolant flow velocity in the center of the water jacket. As a result, the coolant flow velocity at the top of the cylinder bores increases, enhancing the cooling effect at the top of the cylinder block and between the cylinder bores. Furthermore, the area near the center of the cylinder bores is less affected by the coolant, so the wall temperature rises. These reduce the temperature difference on the cylinder bore walls for uniform thermal expansion and lower the viscosity of the engine oil adhering to the bore walls, reducing friction.
The bullet shape of the rear end and the optimized layout of the transmission tightening bolts ensure joint rigidity with the transaxle and improve quietness.
The cover shape around the balance shafts and the optimized layout of the oil drain holes reduce the flow of oil into the balance shaft area, reducing friction caused by engine oil agitation.
The structure has been simplified by building in the air conditioner compressor bracket, oil filter bracket, rear oil seal retainer, balancer bearings, oil pump bracket, rear end plate, etc.
By making the volume of the oil pan bottom large, the oil level is lowered without changing the oil quantity, reducing oil agitation by the balance shafts, etc. and reducing friction.

By adopting a 8mm-pitch roller chain to drive the camshafts, the sprockets have been made smaller in diameter, making the engine more compact. Also, the chain pins have been chrome carburized to ensure wear resistance.
A hydraulic chain tensioner with a ratchet mechanism has been adopted to keep the tension applied to the chain constant. It is mounted externally for serviceability.
An oil jet (integrated with the cylinder block) has been provided to lubricate the timing chain, for quietness and durability.
An aluminum alloy timing chain cover has been adopted, which integrally seals the front of the cylinder block, crankcase and cylinder head.
A tooth skip prevention guide and chain guide are provided on the timing chain cover to prevent valve timing deviation during assembly and servicing.
The RH engine mounting bracket is a separate cast iron part, further reducing engine roll vibration.

VVT-i (Variable Valve Timing-intelligent) has been adopted, which varies the intake valve timing according to driving conditions to achieve both low fuel consumption and high output as well as low emissions.

MECA.TITLE: Valve, Valve Lifter and Valve Spring

ITEM.PTXT: The intake valves and exhaust valves have been nitrided over their entire surface to ensure wear resistance. Also, weight has been reduced by making the stems smaller in diameter.
The exhaust valves have been heat treated (solution aging treatment) to cope with the rise in exhaust temperature due to higher performance.

Shimless type valve lifters with a large effective area have been adopted to accommodate high lift. Also, the top surface has been treated with Fericoat (molybdenum-containing iron phosphate coating) to ensure reliability and reduce friction.
The valve springs use high-strength material and are nitrided for higher strength, and have a thin wire diameter and uneven pitch to improve valve follow-up, achieve high lift and reduce weight.

Valve Lifter Specifications (Common to Intake and Exhaust)

ITEM.PTXT: High-strength alloy cast iron has been adopted for both the intake and exhaust camshafts, and the cam noses have been chill treated to ensure durability. Also, the cam lobes have been made narrower to reduce weight and friction loss. For lubrication of the cam journals, oil is supplied from the oil hole in the center of the camshaft.
The working angle of the intake camshaft has been increased for higher lift, and valve timing has been optimized to increase output.
A vane-type VVT-i controller has been provided on the intake camshaft.
It consists of a housing fixed to the timing gear and a vane fixed to the camshaft.

By applying oil pressure from the OCV (oil control valve) to the advance chamber and retard chamber of the VVT-i controller, the vane is rotated, continuously varying the phase of the intake camshaft.
When the engine is stopped, it is locked at the most retarded position by the lock pin. When the engine starts, the lock pin is released by oil pressure.
The position of the spool valve is controlled by the duty signal from the ECU to regulate the oil supply to the advance and retard chambers of the VVT-i controller.
Lightweight, high-rigidity aluminum alloy pistons have been adopted.
High-strength steel has been adopted for both the connecting rods and connecting rod caps to reduce weight.
Nutless type connecting rod bolts have been adopted to make the big end more compact and stabilize the axial force. Also, plastic region tightening has been adopted for the bolts.
Balance shafts have been adopted to reduce booming noise in the vehicle.

An offset crank, in which the crankshaft center is offset from the cylinder center, has been adopted, reducing friction loss through lower piston side force and improving thermal efficiency through changes in piston speed, for lower fuel consumption.

A forged 5-journal, 8-balance weight crankshaft has been adopted. The crank pins and journals have smaller fillets and narrower widths, ensuring rigidity and reducing friction. Also, improved surface roughness and smaller pin diameters reduce weight and friction.
Eccentric groove bearings have been adopted for the crankshaft bearings, reducing oil leakage from the ends while ensuring oil flow at the center of the bearings, for reduced friction.

ENTRY.PTXT: Center Distance Between Big and Small Ends [mm]

ITEM.PTXT: Piston weight has been reduced by shortening the compression height and using a short skirt. Also, the top has a slant squish structure to optimize fuel economy and volumetric efficiency.
The piston skirt width has been reduced, and a striated finish and resin coating have been applied to reduce friction.
Lightweight piston pins with a short overall length have been adopted.
Compression ring No.1,No.2 has a narrow width to lower tension and reduce friction. Also, compression ring No.1 has been PVD treated to ensure wear resistance.
The oil ring has a lightweight 2-piece construction, reducing friction while ensuring good oil control.

By adopting an offset crank, in which the crankshaft centerline is offset from the cylinder bore centerline, the maximum combustion pressure can be transmitted efficiently. Also, friction loss is reduced by reducing piston side force, and thermal efficiency is improved by changes in piston speed, lowering fuel consumption.
The maximum combustion pressure is efficiently transmitted to the crankshaft, and the thrust force acting on the piston during the combustion stroke is reduced to reduce friction loss.

A region where the piston speed is slower occurs in the first half of the combustion stroke (Fig. 1). As a result, combustion takes place with the piston closer to top dead center, increasing combustion pressure and improving thermal efficiency (Fig. 2).

Eccentric groove bearings have been adopted for the crankshaft bearings. Normally, the clearance at the ends of a bearing is larger than at the center, and the amount of oil leakage is also greater. Eccentric groove bearings reduce oil leakage at the ends while ensuring oil flow at the center, making it possible to reduce the oil pump discharge volume and thereby reducing friction.

Balance shafts have been adopted to cancel the 2-order inertia force that causes increased vibration and noise in large-displacement in-line 4-cylinder engines. Also, by optimizing the inertial mass of the balance shafts, low vibration and quietness (reduced vehicle booming noise) have been improved.
The drive method is direct drive by a gear press-fitted onto the #3 counterweight of the crankshaft.

Plastic gears have been adopted for driven gears No1 and No.3 to suppress gear noise. Also, friction loss has been reduced by making the bearings smaller in diameter, and the shaft length has been shortened, making the balance shafts among the lightest and most compact in the world.
A vertical wall has been formed in the balance shaft housing to reduce the flow of oil into the balance shaft area, reducing friction.

Cylinders No. 1 and No. 4, and cylinders No. 2 and No. 3, are in the same phase as each other and are 180° opposite in phase, so if the piston motion were perfect simple harmonic motion , the reciprocating inertia forces would cancel each other out. In an actual engine, due to the principle of the crank-piston mechanism, the piston speed is greatest on the top dead center side of the middle of the stroke even when the crankshaft rotation speed is constant, so higher-order (distortion) components are generated. These higher-order components occur 2 times per 1 crankshaft revolution, particularly in in-line 4-cylinder engines, and since they do not cancel but overlap each other, they cause increased vibration and noise. This component is the 2-order inertia force.

2 balance shafts are rotated at 2 times the speed of the crankshaft to cancel the 2-order inertia force. Also, by rotating the 2 shafts in opposite directions, the vibration generated by the balance shafts is canceled out.

A serpentine belt drive system, in which all accessories are driven by 1 V-ribbed belt, has been adopted, reducing overall engine length and weight. An automatic tensioner for the V-ribbed belt has been adopted, extending the life of the belt and accessories, making them maintenance-free and improving serviceability when removing and installing the belt.
By lowering the tension of the accessory drive belt, friction has been reduced and fuel economy improved.

A PCV hose and PCV valve are provided to forcibly introduce blow-by gas into the intake system and burn it, preventing blow-by gas containing large amounts of HC from being released into the atmosphere.
Under light load, blow-by gas is drawn into the surge tank by intake manifold vacuum through the PCV valve.
Under heavy load, the introduction of fresh air is stopped to handle a large flow of blow-by gas.
The engine is supported by 4 mounts (front, RH, LH and rear) to reduce noise and vibration.
Dynamic dampers have been adopted on the LH (2WD models, 4WD models) and rear (4WD models) engine mountings to reduce engine noise.
A fluid-filled engine mounting has been adopted for the RH engine mounting and its installation position has been optimized, absorbing vibration efficiently to improve ride comfort.
